_comment: Plain-language layer over the raw feedback API. Keyed by feedback id. `area` groups the board; `plain` is the layman description shown as the row's primary text; `state` is one of open | dark | partial | discuss; `note` is the short state qualifier rendered beside the chip. Authored by Claude, appended each run — see SKILL.md step 3.

205.plain: Not a feature request — three design tenets (simple beats complex; too much information is worse than none; build for people who aren't technical) plus a request to sit down and align on them. He names the trade calculator as the worst offender.

310.plain: Don't lock the manual calculator behind trades; cut the navigation down to just Rank, Calculator and League; and put a value-prop line on both surfaces linking to rankings — 'we can now tailor trades to your exact valuations'.
310.note: calculator unlocked; nav + value-prop not done

331.plain: Make every player tile tappable, opening a card with age, year-by-year stats, per-game numbers, and a weekly game log when you tap into a season.

332.plain: An in-season breakout finder: snap counts and target counts per player, plus a section showing who's trending up and down across opportunity metrics.

337.plain: The Draft tab disappeared from the Acquire tab while a draft was actually live — the bottom navigation was still showing it. The two disagree.

338.plain: 'Send in Sleeper' delivered the trade, but the other owner never got a Sleeper direct message about it.

342.plain: The give side and the get side of a suggested trade card aren't the same size, and the gaps between them are uneven.

343.plain: The leaderboard is showing Greg with an absurdly large number.

344.plain: Too many settings stacked on one flat layer — group them into nested pages.

345.plain: Delete the 'more ways to rank' sheet and make that button go straight to Build Your Board.

347.plain: The trade tiles don't show which tier each player belongs to.

348.plain: Player names are cut off on the trade tiles — show the full name.

349.plain: Draft picks on the tiles don't show the pick number.

350.plain: The same two or three players keep reappearing across suggestion after suggestion, because the app prices them too high. Same guy, bad package, over and over.
350.note: one of four reports on suggestion quality

351.plain: Jordan Tyson came off the board at 1.01 in a mock — implausible enough to point at a valuation problem.

352.plain: Let users like and dislike individual players so favourites surface more often and unwanted ones stop appearing — and the same control by position.

353.plain: Add each player's NFL draft position to the tiles.

354.plain: You can lock your own players into a package so they stay put, but the lock button is missing on the opponent's players.

356.plain: 2026 picks show as a generic '2026 2nd' instead of the real slot the pick actually is, like 2.05.

360.plain: Add an 'avoiding' row beside shopping-for and willing-to-sell: positions you never want sent to you at all.

361.plain: Follow-up to #360 — he grants he could just pick the positions he does want, but says the no-flag is cheap because the logic already exists.

363.plain: 'Tier up' came back as nothing but one-for-one swaps, a lot of them low-value players only worth a 2nd or 3rd.

365.plain: Your contend-or-rebuild window is judged on roster age alone — he's all-in in FFV3 and the app calls him a rebuilder. Suggests counting first-round picks owned versus traded away as a second signal.

370.plain: Trades you already liked in an earlier session come back around again in a new one.

371.plain: Let playoff odds be the primary decider for the contend-or-rebuild window, rather than a side input.

372.plain: Age distribution alone is too weak a signal — fold in starter dynasty value and playoff likelihood, and keep age as a lighter driver.
372.note: built · flag trade.outlook_composite off AND not in any shipped build

382.plain: The team order doesn't match the pick values shown next to them — he suspects a pick-value adjustment issue.

385.plain: Quick stats on each player without leaving the screen — baseline points per game, where they finished the season, maybe a wins-above-replacement style number.

387.plain: The page spends too much room on other information. He wants mockups for a redesign that gives the rankings themselves more of the screen.
387.note: asks for mockups, not a build

388.plain: Add a minimised league-ranks view — the little bar-graph thumbnail — to this page and make it the primary home again, which is what frees up room on the rankings page.

389.plain: Remove the free agents and draft links.

390.plain: Swap one of the tiles for playoff projections.

392.plain: On a first visit the screen implies trades are already being found in the background, but nothing actually runs until you press 'Find a trade'.

393.plain: Rank and evaluate trade cards the way League Home already identifies buyers and sellers: target the positions you're weakest at from the teams deepest there, while the package you give up comes from your surplus and fills their hole. He calls this by far the strongest way to produce trades that actually get accepted.
393.note: his own proposed fix for the suggestion-quality cluster

399.plain: The avatar on 'filter the league by one position' faces the wrong way and should be flipped.

400.plain: Take 'Getting too much' out of the list of reasons for declining a trade.

401.plain: Stop suggesting trades that swap similarly valued players at the same position — 'trim the fluff a bit'.

402.plain: Change what the 'more offers' button does: instead of its current behaviour, drop the user to tier-up and tier-down choices presented inline below the trade chip.
402.note: ruled 2026-08-27: #402+#403 are one experience — rev-2 docs + mockups in docs/feedback/items/402-more-offers-shop/

403.plain: Let users 'shop' a player: pick someone, then choose to tier up, tier down, or explore same-value swaps at positions you select. Offers come back as small tiles or as swipeable cards with a '1 of X' counter, each carrying its own like and dismiss button. He is explicit that this is an idea, not a design yet.

404.plain: 'Add a league' in the header dropdown drops you on the ranking page instead of the add-a-league flow.
